names: regional large-load demand and reliable-capacity scarcity

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: dispatchable generation and power-market access are scarce infrastructure needed for reliable large-load growth

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: renewables/storage, new gas/nuclear and grid expansion can compete over time, but near-term reliable capacity remains constrained

adversarial-red-team.name: financing risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: substantial debt-market activity is balanced by strong liquidity and operating cash flow

adversarial-red-team.name: commodity/market exposure
adversarial-red-team.basis: earnings depend on realized power/capacity economics and hedging as well as physical availability

expectations-execution.name: operating execution and reliability

factors: regional large-load demand and reliable-capacity scarcity

items.risk: Power-market exposure, acquisition integration, permitting and large-load project timing can alter realized economics.
GAAP earnings remain sensitive to hedge mark-to-market movements and realized power prices.
Permitting, interconnection, commodity prices and data-center project timing can prevent scarcity from converting into expected contracted economics.
Debt/refinancing and commodity collateral requirements can amplify downside in stressed power markets.
Helix/data-center optionality can be overcapitalized before committed MW and project economics are visible.
Acquisition integration and plant incidents/outages can reduce expected fleet cash generation.
Commodity-market volatility can increase collateral posting requirements and consume otherwise available liquidity even when long-run demand remains favorable.
items.observedBasis: $1.874B cash/eligible assets and $3.006B letters of credit posted for commodity hedging/trading at June 30, 2026.

items.risk: Additional hybrid/debt issuance can increase fixed or quasi-fixed capital claims and refinancing complexity; the September 2026 junior subordinated issuance is evidence of continued capital-market use, not evidence of distress by itself.

Large computational loads can disconnect abruptly and create reliability-management requirements; regulatory/interconnection responses may change how quickly or under what conditions new load converts into generator demand and economics.
